A lightweight native Android client for the DeepSeek API.

ShallowDrop is an independent client adapted from the open-source DeepSeek chat demo. It is not an official DeepSeek app. Much of the project code was created with AI assistance.

API access, availability and billing are governed by the service provider. This project does not provide API credits or guarantee the availability of external services.

AI-generated answers may contain errors. Verify information before relying on it for important decisions.

Sending messages, uploading attachments and using voice or location features sends the relevant data to the API service. Only submit information you are authorized to share. Chat history is stored locally; export a backup before uninstalling the app or clearing its data.

The software is provided as is under its applicable open-source licenses, to the extent permitted by law. Copyright notices, license terms and warranty disclaimers are available in Open-source licenses.
MIT applies to project code unless a file states otherwise. The components below retain their own licenses.

Draw a pelican riding a bicycle. Make it look like it\'s really trying.
Pelican legs are short and the webbed feet can\'t reach the pedals. Lower the saddle all the way, and keep the beak clear of the handlebars.

Done 🚲

- **Pose**: leaning forward, wings resting on the handlebars
- **Feet**: planted on the pedals, saddle at its lowest
- **Beak**: a water bottle tucked in the pouch for the long ride
The feathers look like plastic, the knees bend the wrong way, and the beak is too short. I review pelican art eight hours a day, at least a hundred bikes a day. You can\'t fool me.

Got it, one by one:

1. **Feathers**: added fine down and shafts in the backlight, no more shine
2. **Joints**: the part that seems to bend backwards is the ankle; the real knee hides under the feathers
3. **Beak**: now a third of the body length, with the pouch bouncing on bumps

If it's still not right, I'll draw another one.

New idea: this time the pelican rides a tandem, with a fish on the back seat.\n\nFeathers, joints and beak all keep your notes. Honestly, there\'s no perfect solution yet, but this one **at least won\'t crash**.

Version three:

- Helmet and knee pads, which conveniently cover the disputed joints
- The long beak kept scraping the front wheel, so it got a mudguard
- Feathers redone with the texture you asked for

I doubt anyone studies pelicans on bikes harder than you do.
